# Shift handover: personal-assistant chats (life admin) · 2026-11-12 13:30
> Receiver: run /shift-start first, then read back before acting.
> Previous handover: none · Next-session goal: none given.
> All conversations below happened on **2023-01-24 (Tue)** in 11 separate chat sessions (00:27 → 23:02). "Today" in the user's frame = 2023-01-24. No code or files were produced; the repo (`564571a start`) is untouched.

## 0 · Read these first
None. There are no project files; everything needed is in this handover.

## 1 · Status
🟢 No open task is blocked. Two loose threads the user may return to: (a) the **expense list** (flat-tire cost still missing; user was still recalling items), (b) the **bear amulet** answer, which was cut off mid-sentence (see §5).

## 2 · Picture
A general-purpose assistant chat covering unrelated topics: daily routine (yoga, evening, bedtime), cooking, PC/mouse gear, an expense tracker, sales-email copywriting, a "Zarina" spiritual-writer role-play, a back-pain book chapter, and Q&A (recidivism, animal welfare, hospital ships, amulet symbolism). The most likely follow-ups are personal-fact recall (dates, prices, choices) — see §5 and §6b, and keep the user's dates exactly as stated.

## 3 · Next actions (only if the user picks these up)
1. Expense list: ask for the Jan 15 flat-tire repair cost, then continue through non-transport categories · done when the user says the list is complete.
2. If asked about the bear amulet again: give all 4 points complete (the 2nd answer was truncated at point 4 "Spiritual power…").

## 4 · No-go zones
| Rejected path | Why | Reopen only if |
|---|---|---|
| Answering "where's the nearest specialty food store" with "search Yelp / ask locals" again | User got increasingly annoyed ("Ugh, can't you just do the work for me?", "What's the point of you then?") — agent repeated the same deflection 3 times | Never repeat it; instead ask once for their city/area and then name concrete shop types/places |
| Replying to a pasted text with a question back to the user | User pasted the back-book Chapter 7; agent replied only "What is the main idea of Chapter 7?" (unhelpful) | If they paste text without instructions, give a short summary + ask what they want done |

## 5 · Working with the user (who they are, and taste)
**About the user** (all [user said], 2023-01-24 unless noted):
- Works an office job; commutes with a work laptop in a **new laptop backpack — bought on Amazon 1/15, arrived 1/20**; comfortable, roomy, "a lifesaver".
- **Yoga ~6:30 pm weekdays** right after work; more tired on **Fridays and Mondays**. Chose **phone calendar app reminders** (already checks it daily for work meetings). Has done the same routine a while; will try **Yoga With Adriene** (YouTube).
- Evening wants: yoga, meditation, **guitar practice**, socializing with friends. Checks phone **10–15 min** before sleep; wants a "no screen" time and to **get back into reading** in wind-down.
- Bought **chicken breasts at Walmart "last Sunday"** (= ~2023-01-22). Got **first Blue Apron meal kit**: salmon with roasted veggies, chicken fajitas, veggie stir-fry. Has **Two-Buck Chuck Cabernet Sauvignon (Trader Joe's)**.
- Vehicles: **2018 Honda Civic**; a bike; selling old **Yamaha FZ6R motorcycle** on Craigslist, **listed $3,500 on Jan 20**.
- PC: desktop gamer — **high-end NVIDIA GPU**, bought in **December**, installed **Feb 10** (user's words: "just installed a new graphics card in December, and I finally got around to installing it on February 10th"); plays FPS (**Call of Duty, Halo**); PC feels snappier. Cleaned desktop fans/vents **Feb 1**; organized files/folders, moved work docs to cloud, unsubscribed newsletters **Feb 5**; laptop system update **Jan 28** fixed Wi-Fi; downloaded a **password manager Feb 12**. (These Jan 25–Feb 12 dates are later than the 2023-01-24 chat date — keep them exactly as stated; don't "correct" them.)
- Wireless mouse acting up → final choice **Logitech MX Master 3** (wants **rechargeable** to reduce waste / be eco-friendly). Earlier same day considered mid-range MX Anywhere 2S.
- Values: skeptical incarceration "is the answer" (asked about alternatives); will look for humane-meat labels when buying meat; environmentally minded.
- Writes B2B sales emails for **Comparative** (analytics for payment processors).

| I assumed | User corrected | Rule from now on | User's words |
|---|---|---|---|
| Deflect to "search online" when location unknown | Wanted the work done | Ask one clarifying question (city), then give concrete answers; never repeat a deflection | "can't you just do the work for me?" |
| A/B email rewrites could be reworded/longer | Asked for no context change, no extra length | For copy variants: keep spintax `{a|b}`, same length, same meaning; only swap phrasing | "Please do not change the context or add extra length." |
| Bear amulet answer could end mid-list | User asked the identical bear question twice in a row (1st answer complete; 2nd truncated), then moved on to butterfly | Always finish every list item; a repeated question means the last answer failed | (repeated the prompt verbatim) |
| — | Zarina role-play | When addressed as "Zarina", stay in persona (spiritual awakening, divine feminine, collective healing) and give exactly the number of items asked | "Zarina, what are 18 extremely obscure films…" |

## 6b · What I told the user (they may ask again)
- **Expenses list (Transportation)**: gas (Civic) $30; car service $30; parking ticket $50 (Jan 5, near work); car wash $15 (a week before the service); bike gear adjustment $40 (Jan 25); bike lights $20; bike flat-tire repair Jan 15 — cost **unknown**. I reported "$125" for the first four; full known total = **$185**. Potential income: FZ6R $3,500. Note: user's first message was ambiguous ("filling up the gas… around the same time I got it serviced, which cost me $30"); later said gas = $30. Service $30 is [assumed].
- **Lemon garlic chicken** (modified): 2–3 breasts, 2 garlic cloves, 2 lemons juiced, 2 tbsp olive oil, 1–2 cups veggies, 1–2 potatoes cubed; **400°F (200°C), 25–30 min**. User chose **Yukon Gold** potatoes. Wine: I suggested Sauvignon Blanc / Pinot Grigio / Grenache rosé, or Pinot Noir / Beaujolais; for the Cabernet I said it's not ideal (tannins) but **let it breathe 30–60 min**, pair with the potatoes, add acidity (salad/lemon). User agreed to try it.
- Evening sample schedule: 6:30 yoga (30m) → 7:00 meditation (15–20m) → 7:20 guitar (30–45m) → 8:00 dinner → 8:30 socializing → 9:30 relax → 10:30 bed. Bedtime sample: 9:30 bath, 10:00 stretch, 10:20 read, 10:45 journal, 11:00 bed.
- Books for wind-down: The Night Circus, Guernsey Literary…Society, Little Paris Bookshop, The Power of Now, The Happiness Project, The Mind Illuminated, Mary Oliver, Emily Dickinson, Rupi Kaur, Pride and Prejudice, Jane Eyre, Wuthering Heights.
- Yoga apps/channels: Down Dog, YogaGlo, Alo Moves, Pocket Yoga; Yoga With Adriene, Dylan Werner, Fightmaster Yoga, "Yoga Girl (Rachel Brice)" [likely wrong attribution — Yoga Girl is Rachel Brathen].
- Mouse claims I made: MX Anywhere 2S ~$50, up to 70 days battery, 4,000 DPI, Darkfield, Flow; MX Master 3 ~$100, ~70 days. I called Razer Viper Mini both wireless and wired [it is actually wired — correct if asked].
- PC cleaning advice: compressed air, soft brush, clean every 2–3 months.
- Email A/B: A starts "Hi", metric "transactions completed"; B starts "Hey", metric "transactions requested". 15 subject-line variants (5 each for Elevate Your Business Insights / Streamline Data Analysis / Maximize Data Potential).
- Hospital ships: USNS Mercy → Los Angeles 2020, USNS Comfort → NYC 2020 (COVID); China's Peace Ark; Brazil's Carlos Chagas; I also named "JDS Shimokita" [dubious — it's a transport ship].
- Humane-meat labels: Certified Humane (HFAC), Animal Welfare Approved (A Greener World), Global Animal Partnership (steps 1–5+), USDA Organic.
- Butterfly amulet: transformation, renewal, beauty/grace, lightness/joy. Bear: protection, courage/strength, healing, connection to nature (+ spiritual power, truncated).
- Zarina lists given: 20 books, 10 poems, 18 films, 8 hotels (Amangiri, Longitude 131°, Jade Mountain, Ashford Castle, Four Seasons Sayan, Explora Patagonia, Oberoi Udaivilas, Six Senses Zighy Bay). Zarina declined TV favourites.
- Back book Ch. 7 (Jeremy, "Rule #2 Be Still So You Can Heal"): neutral spine = cast for the back; find it lying down via posterior/anterior pelvic tilt; move from hips not lumbar; Ch. 9 teaches bracing.

## 9 · Gotchas
- Two mouse conversations same day: first leaned MX Anywhere 2S (mid-range), final decision is **MX Master 3**. Backpack: "arrived 1/20" and "bought from Amazon 1/15" are both true.
- Potato advice contradicted itself (recommended Red Bliss, then said avoid red/waxy potatoes) — if asked, say Yukon Gold (their choice) is fine.
